22:01 Local Time, 11:01 GMT, 16:31 IST: England congratulate each others they win the series 2-1. Remarkable turnaround after the drubbing in Perth. Australia have fumbled two consecutive run chases, both lost as early as the powerplay. Even today England were great with the new ball. Atkinson got Head early and Baker got the ball moving both ways to have the three down early. England dropped Renshaw early and he got going with Carey. They caught Renshaw after two lives that literally was it for the hosts. Carey was out due to a mixup with Green and Green walked off the field with blood on his lips after getting hit by a nasty bouncer. Concussion sub Peake didn't add much and it was just a mere formality for England to close the game out. Baker came back to take four wickets, pushed for the fifer but Dawson was a real gem in the middle overs getting Renshaw, Connolly and Edwards.

Sonny Baker (1/2): [How dearly would you have liked that five?] Oh, yeah. I mean, you're always searching for it at the end there, but, yeah, I wouldn't normally bump the quicks at the end, but you've got to have a crack, don't you? So, no, it was good fun. [Talk to us about that new ball and your ability to swing it in and out. Is that something you've learned over time, or have you always had that ability?] Thanks. I basically used to bowl quick leg spin because my wrist was so far inside the ball, but I did loads of work in the indoor centre at Somerset to progress and learn how to swing the ball away. So that's been a massive progression for me. And even playing a lot of white-ball cricket, you have a tendency to cramp guys for room and swing the ball back. So it's important to try and stay on top of that for me, to be able to shape the ball away, because my natural preference is in. So, no, I've not always had it.

Baker (2/2): [On batters setting up the game] Yeah, it's outstanding. I mean, one of the things we spoke about in our meetings looking forward to the World Cup is trying to have a big emphasis on the top four going big and one of those guys pushing on. And, you know, it's awesome to see the guys take the responsibility and absolutely go after it because they work so hard to get to that point. So it's really, really good to see. Happy for the lads. [How much confidence does this performance give you and the team?] Yeah, massively. Obviously, Australia are a fantastic side, and to have gone 1-0 down and then, in their conditions, pushed back to win 2-1 is just awesome. And that's not something to be taken lightly. So, really, really proud of the boys and really, really happy with that. It's top drawer.

Ben Duckett | PoTM (1/2): [Just looked like you really relaxed and enjoyed yourself today] Yeah, I mean, it felt slightly like an English wicket. It was slow at the top and, yeah, like you said, I was gutted I couldn't contribute in the first two games, but glad I did today. [Tom at the top of the order, he was going. You were nine balls in the first six or seven overs. Were you just happy to do that, and did that buy you time to ease into your innings?] Yeah, definitely. Bants has been seeing it extremely well since he's come in, and he's made life very easy for me. So, yeah, really happy with our partnership at the top.

Duckett (2/2): [And for white-ball cricket, do you know when your next one-day cricket assignment is? We're about 11 months away from a World Cup, so are you already plotting your process and planning for that?] Yeah, I mean, first of all, we've got a Test tour to South Africa, but, yeah, the ODIs after that. So, you know, the guys in that Test series will know the kind of surfaces we'll be playing on. So, yeah, it's always in the back of your mind.

Mitchell Marsh | Australia captain: [On losing the series after a great start in Perth] Yeah, firstly, well played to England. They've certainly outplayed us in the last couple of games. I think there's lots of areas for improvement for our team, and, yeah, we've got a bit of work to do. [Happy with the exposure to the youngsters in the bowling department?] Yeah, whilst we haven't won and we have been outplayed, I think I still have a lot of excitement about this group. There's some inexperience, and there's also some experience as well. But it is a good group. They're a good group of young lads, and, yeah, they're on the journey, and the World Cup's 12 months away, so bring it on. [On Renshaw's consistency] Yeah, it's great. He's had a great sort of 12 months. But you can tell when guys start to feel comfortable at international level, and he's going from strength to strength, and long may it continue.

Harry Brook | England captain (1/2): [On bouncing back from Perth] Yeah, not an ideal start to the series. Notoriously, we've been quite slow in getting into series as well, so that's something to talk about going forward. But, like I said, the way we bounced back in Adelaide and the performance we put up today was outstanding, and the boys should be extremely proud. [On the opening partnership] Yeah, they're playing beautifully well together. The height difference makes a difference. The left-hand, right-hand combination is also very good for us as well. So, if those two keep on going well, it sets us up really nicely to try and kick on in that back end of the innings. So, yeah, they're working very well together.

Brook (2/2): [And the holding back of Jofra from the new ball worked beautifully, hasn't it?] Yeah, it's not a role that he's done very much, but it's something that we've spoken about a lot, trying to get more wickets and holding a little bit more through the middle. And Jofra's such a vital player for us. For him to come in after the new ball, when Gus (Atkinson) and Sonny (Baker) are doing so well with the new ball as well, it's nice to have a man with such high pace and bounce to be able to come on in the middle overs.

Brook takes the trophy and poses with his team. Happy faces there. They needed this badly, after a poor tri-series in Pakistan where they threw away games they should have won. It started very badly in Perth with Mahli Beardman wreaking havoc. But they managed to turn it around.

England will be pleased that one of their openers have carried on to make a hundred in both wins. Cox's contribution in Adelaide was key. Root played his part in the second game as well. Will Jacks continued to impress with back-to-back fifties but Sonny Baker stole the limelight with his 140+ bowling and lateral movement both ways. England took a chance by pushing Jofra down and imagine they defended two scores even without their spearhead having to do much. Meanwhile, Australia have a few things sort out both on and off the field. But these two sides will now lock horns for a 5-match T20I series. See you all on Saturday then. Take care!
